title: Yukon coroner will hold inquest in police shooting near Whitehorse airport
article: The Yukon Coroner's Service will hold an inquest into the death of the man shot by an RCMP officer at an Air North hangar near Whitehorse's airport in November 2022.

According to a March 19 notice from the coroner's service, it has been investigating the death of Hugh Errol Riffel since November 2022. According to the notice an inquest into the facts of the death is scheduled to commence Oct. 6, 2025 at a Whitehorse courtroom. It is being ordered pursuant to the section of the Coroner's Act that requires inquests when people die in police custody.

The presiding coroner will hear evidence to determine the facts and circumstances of Riffel's death. A jury will be present and will have an opportunity to make recommendations aimed at preventing deaths in similar circumstances.
Chief Coroner Heather Jones confirmed that the incident the inquest will be looking into was the police\-involved shooting at the Air North facility on Nov. 24, 2022.

The incident was previously investigated by the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team, an independent organization that investigates serious incidents involving police officers. ASIRT has been under contract to investigate incidents in the Yukon since 2011.

The officer in question was cleared by the police watchdog with investigation results released in September 2024. The investigation report explains that the man police shot, not identified by name in that report, was armed with a .22 calibre rifle which he pointed at both an employee at the Air North facility and himself but it failed to fire when he pulled the trigger in both cases.

ASIRT's investigation found that the man also struck another employee in the face, tried to point the gun at him and threatened to kill him. The man fired the gun into the air after police arrived. According to ASIRT he then walked towards RCMP officers with the rifle in hand, telling them to shoot him. An officer shot him when he was about 10 metres from police. Per the ASIRT report the incident was captured on video. The man was taken to hospital where he died.
